title: Voice-controlled computer use for the Mac
summary: Dictate a command and the Mac starts acting on it before the sentence is finished.
how_jev_is_used: Jev reads the transcript as it streams in and picks the next on-screen action, fast enough that the app opens mid-sentence.

title: jevmeter: a live BS meter for any video
summary: Scores every sentence of a video against a set of yes/no questions and renders the result as an on-screen meter.
how_jev_is_used: Each sentence goes to Jev with five yes/no questions. The author reports 1,191 calls for a full presidential debate at a total cost of about five cents.

title: JEV: how it works and what you can build
summary: Riley Brown walks through how Jev works and builds with it on screen.
how_jev_is_used: A practical tour of routing, classifying and filtering with Jev, and why a model that can't write is useful inside software.

title: Hide posts on X with plain-language rules
summary: A browser extension that collapses posts on X matching rules written in everyday language.
how_jev_is_used: Each post in the feed is checked by Jev against the rules. The author reports it is fast enough to go unnoticed and very cheap to run.

title: Model router
summary: Sends each request to whichever model suits it best.
how_jev_is_used: Jev reads the incoming request and chooses the model from a list; the request is then forwarded to that model.

title: Jev Router on OpenRouter
summary: A packaged router on OpenRouter that picks the model and reasoning effort for each request.
how_jev_is_used: Before each turn, Jev scores the prompt on difficulty and precision and checks whether a cheaper or stronger model fits, balancing quality, speed and cost.

title: jev-drone: a camera-only autonomous drone
summary: A simulated quadrotor that flies an obstacle course using only its onboard camera.
how_jev_is_used: Jev runs at about 2.5 times a second and decides what the current situation means; time-critical flight control stays in ordinary code. The author built the first version in 15 minutes for 10 cents.

title: Jev: the ultimate classification model?
summary: Sam Witteveen tests Jev on a range of classification tasks and looks at how it differs from LLMs.
how_jev_is_used: Covers Jev's System One approach, its speed, and where fast classification fits in real workflows.

title: Fast app testing with OpenCode
summary: A demo of an AI agent clicking through an app under test at high speed.
how_jev_is_used: Jev makes the step-by-step choices of what to click next, so the testing agent doesn't wait on a large model for every action.

title: Jev Review: staged code review
summary: A code-review workflow for diffs or whole codebases, with a quiet local dashboard.
how_jev_is_used: Code orchestrates the review; Jev handles bounded judgements at each stage: a risk matrix, file profiles, evidence selection and severity scores.

title: jevgrep: find code by asking what it does
summary: A CLI that points coding agents at the right files for an unfamiliar task.
how_jev_is_used: Jev judges relevance across folders, files and declarations, and returns files and verbatim excerpts. The author reports the same 8 of 10 SWE-bench tasks solved at about 30% lower cost.

title: What is Jev and how to use it?
summary: A developer tutorial on what Jev is and how to call it from an application.
how_jev_is_used: Explains structured decisions and walks through using Jev in code, step by step.

title: jgrep: grep where the pattern is a description
summary: Filters lines of text by meaning, for example 'a user is getting frustrated' in a live log.
how_jev_is_used: Each line becomes one yes/no question to Jev; the author reports about 200 ms and a thousandth of a cent per line.

title: Jevmail: open-source Gmail triage
summary: Sorts a Gmail inbox into Needs reply, Updates, Promos, Sales and Spam, read-only and running locally.
how_jev_is_used: Jev classifies each message and gives an urgency score; the author reports 1,000 emails in about a minute for around three cents.

title: Jev plays Super Mario Bros.
summary: An agent that plays the original Super Mario Bros. from emulator data, not screenshots.
how_jev_is_used: Game memory is turned into a compact description of Mario, enemies and terrain, and Jev chooses one legal controller action at a time.

title: Shapeshift: an input that becomes what you mean
summary: One text box that turns into an event card, checklist, timer, bill splitter and more as you type.
how_jev_is_used: One Jev call answers 14 questions about what you typed; dates, amounts and maths are handled by code. Works offline with a fallback classifier.

title: A client follow-up agent with Jev matching requests
summary: An agent built on an open harness that matches client requests to the right GitHub issue.
how_jev_is_used: The author reports 40 requests matched as accurately as when Opus made every match, with decision cost about 150 times lower.

title: A data analyst agent with Jev as the reviewer
summary: A plain-English data agent that checks its own work.
how_jev_is_used: Qwen writes the SQL and explains results, Jev acts as the review layer, and Vercel's eve runs the loop and the human approval flow.

title: Jev Spider: Jev rearranges a website's layout
summary: A demo where Jev decides the size, colour and position of page components.
how_jev_is_used: It rearranges the components based on its own preference.

title: Jevspresso: Jev as a barista
summary: A state-machine demo where XState decides what is possible and Jev decides the next move.
how_jev_is_used: You can order in plain language or break things and watch Jev cope.

title: Jev use cases for AI agents
summary: Where Jev fits in AI agents: picking decisions instead of writing like an LLM.
how_jev_is_used: Shows agent steps handed to Jev and what that saves.

title: Jev plugin for DeepSeek Harness
summary: A native DeepSeek Harness plugin with twelve Jev-powered features.
how_jev_is_used: Jev selects skills and files, supervises tasks, filters tool output and assists with single-operation approvals; each feature can be switched on separately.

title: Building with TypeSafe Jev: patterns from 150+ projects
summary: An unofficial skill that teaches coding agents to design for Jev, with prior art from community projects.
how_jev_is_used: Gives the agent typed-question patterns and links to 150+ community builds sorted by how they use Jev, each with a code sketch.

title: Quicksilver: hand bulk judgement calls to Jev
summary: A Claude Code skill that offloads 'which of these matter?' questions to Jev.
how_jev_is_used: Instead of reading hundreds of files or log lines, Claude asks Jev to sort them and gets back a shortlist with confidence. The author reports 86% fewer Claude tokens on a 12-task benchmark.

title: Claude x Jev: Jev sorts, Claude writes
summary: A free Claude Code skill that pairs Jev's fast decisions with Claude's writing.
how_jev_is_used: Commands let Jev classify, pre-sort items so Claude reads only the uncertain ones, and run a quick safety check before tool calls.

title: Jevlint: a linter for code taste
summary: A linter that checks code against rules written in plain language.
how_jev_is_used: It uses Tree-sitter to pull out code units and asks a decision backend such as Jev whether each one passes.

title: Jev by TypeSafe AI: what is a System-1 decision model
summary: A long-form CampusX session on why Jev is a different kind of model from autoregressive LLMs.
how_jev_is_used: An in-depth lecture on how Jev answers without streaming tokens, and what that changes for latency, cost and reliability.

title: Jevry: a desktop browser that acts on a task
summary: An open-source desktop browser that carries out website tasks, cited research and supported games.
how_jev_is_used: Actions are visible and can be stopped or redirected, and results are grounded in the page.

title: Luna plans, Jev acts: playing poker
summary: A demo from Browser Use pairing a planner model with Jev as the actor.
how_jev_is_used: Luna sets the plan and Jev makes the moves in a poker game.

title: CAPTCHA rebuilt with Jev
summary: A bot check based on how you fill in a form.
how_jev_is_used: The browser measures the behaviour, the server turns it into plain sentences and Jev decides person or bot. The author published a blog post with the source code.

title: CodexQA Jev Browser
summary: Browser automation for checking code after it's written, without sending screenshots to a vision model.
how_jev_is_used: Controls are found from an index of the page and Jev chooses which one to use; part of the CodexQA set of agent skills.

title: jev4pg: semantic operators for PostgreSQL
summary: 41 Jev-powered operators for filtering, extracting, ranking and matching data in PostgreSQL.
how_jev_is_used: Natural-language queries in English and Chinese run as Jev judgements, with caching and reviewable fallbacks.

title: Jev model is a game changer
summary: Piyush Garg explains what Jev is and how it differs from OpenAI and Claude models.
how_jev_is_used: A developer-focused comparison of decision models and chat models, with examples.

title: ldraw-nova: an agent that builds LEGO models
summary: Agent tooling that takes a model idea and produces an LDraw LEGO model.
how_jev_is_used: The agents are built with GPT and Claude models and use Jev for fast decisions. The output includes the LDraw source, 3D and VR views and an editable Blender file.

title: stuntd: a local proxy that learns your typed decisions
summary: A self-hosted proxy that records the typed decisions an app makes and learns to answer them itself.
how_jev_is_used: It speaks the Jev System One protocol and OpenAI's Decisions API, so an app can point at it instead of a hosted model.

title: laya-jev-GraphRAG: an agentic layer for your graph database
summary: A graph-database-agnostic GraphRAG framework with a swappable decision layer.
how_jev_is_used: The decision layer can use local Laya or cloud Jev, so the graph database keeps its role and the framework adds the choices.

title: Jev explained in 17 minutes, with code
summary: A code-along that explains Jev and why a model that cannot write text is useful.
how_jev_is_used: Notes that Jev cannot generate text or code, reports the creator's speed and cost claims and runs examples.

title: Mikey No Code: Jev for beginners
summary: A beginner tutorial on how to set up and use Jev.
how_jev_is_used: Covers getting started with TypeSafe's API.

title: GitButler: what is Jev, and is Laya better?
summary: A comparison of the hosted Jev API with two local decision models.
how_jev_is_used: Runs Laya and Kev locally next to Jev to compare them.

title: Edward Donner: Jev tested against Luna
summary: A test of whether Jev is better, faster and cheaper than a language model.
how_jev_is_used: Compares Jev with Luna on cost and speed.

title: LeJudge: plain-English rules for a world-model planner
summary: An experiment putting Jev inside a JEPA world-model planner.
how_jev_is_used: The planner imagines 300 futures, each is described in words, Jev answers whether it breaks the rule and code adds a penalty. No LLM is involved.

title: A 404 page that fixes your typos
summary: A 404 page that redirects to the page you meant.
how_jev_is_used: Built with Jev, it works out the correct address from the mistyped one.

title: Finding sensitive files on a file share
summary: A security demo where Jev picks out sensitive files.
how_jev_is_used: The author says Jev is very quick at it.

title: jev-ui-test: UI tests in plain language
summary: A UI test framework where test cases are written as sentences and run with pytest.
how_jev_is_used: A browser agent runs each test, and Jev scores the candidate elements to choose every action, with no selectors or site scripts. The author measures about 458 ms per decision.

title: Warren Duffer: intraday trading on Indian stocks
summary: An experimental intraday bot for Nifty 50 stocks through Zerodha or Kotak.
how_jev_is_used: Jev classifies and ranks the stocks and decides take-profit; code sizes each trade, places the stop and enforces the loss limit.

title: jevmem: say it once to Claude Code
summary: Saves decisions and rules from Claude Code chats and brings the relevant ones back next session.
how_jev_is_used: Jev picks which saved notes apply and checks commands and edits against your saved rules before they run.

title: jev-seo: a live SEO audit from one homepage URL
summary: An audit tool that crawls a site, checks it against 52 rules and produces PDF, Excel and Markdown reports.
how_jev_is_used: Jev answers typed questions about every page, and ordinary code scores and ranks the fixes. It runs as a Claude Code skill or from the command line.

title: mu: a coding agent with a judgment kernel
summary: A coding agent that hands its routine judgment calls to a small, fast model.
how_jev_is_used: Jev acts as the judge for decision points such as what stays in context, whether a command is safe and when the work is done, so the large model spends its effort on the code.

title: Astra-Ares: adaptive reasoning effort for Codex
summary: A reference implementation that adjusts how hard GPT-6 reasons during Codex tasks.
how_jev_is_used: Jev decides how much reasoning effort each step needs, to reduce token use. The author describes it as an experimental early preview that runs a patched Codex CLI.

title: system1-agents: agents powered by decision models
summary: A set of ready-made agents for browser use, computer use, games and robotics.
how_jev_is_used: Claude Code or Codex runs a prebuilt agent or builds a new one on Jev, Laya or Cua-S1. The authors report up to 6 times faster and 25 times cheaper than a chat model at the same score.

title: System One for TypeScript: write the decision once
summary: A small provider-neutral TypeScript runtime for bounded AI decisions.
how_jev_is_used: Code uses the same choice, noul and score calls and can run on Jev, a local model or any compatible endpoint.

title: Aayan's YC indexor: search 6,241 startups by description
summary: A search app where matching Y Combinator company logos float up as you describe a startup.
how_jev_is_used: Companies are searchable by what they do, what their logo looks like and what the logo says, and results show how likely each match is. It needs an Apple Silicon Mac.

title: JEV-Star: real-time StarCraft II control
summary: A research project on real-time StarCraft II macro control, plus Jev and GPT micromanagement.
how_jev_is_used: The repository has a paper, five macro configurations and videos of complete games at original speed.

title: ZazenCodes: understanding Jev
summary: A twenty-minute explainer on what Jev is and how to use it.
how_jev_is_used: A twenty-minute walkthrough of what Jev is and why it matters.

title: Cloud Codes: a Jev-style model on your own GPU
summary: A tutorial on running a Jev-style decision model locally.
how_jev_is_used: Makes the case that classifying private data locally avoids sending it to someone else's servers.

title: Automatic note tagging for Obsidian with Jev
summary: A system that tags notes in Obsidian automatically using Jev.
how_jev_is_used: The author, writing in Japanese, shares the setup for other Obsidian users.

title: A free internal linking tool
summary: A tool that finds internal links for a site of up to 500 pages.
how_jev_is_used: Jev classifies and selects the links and the tool outputs a CSV or JSON for an LLM to apply. You bring your own key or pay $1.

title: A live sales copilot
summary: A copilot that listens to a sales call and suggests what to say next.
how_jev_is_used: It tracks the call stage, follows the script, handles objections and shows live signals and a probability of closing.

title: On-device voice pipeline with Jev picking the models
summary: A demo that turns voice memos into to-do lists and meetings into redacted transcripts.
how_jev_is_used: Models for language detection, transcription and removing personal data run on the device, and Jev makes about 20 decisions in one call to choose which to run.

title: jev-leftpad
summary: Left-pads a string using a model call. For reasons.
how_jev_is_used: A deliberately absurd npm package: Jev chooses how many spaces to add from a list of options.

title: Jeview: see every Jev call live
summary: A local gateway that records and visualises every Jev call your code makes.
how_jev_is_used: Point your Jev client at Jeview; it forwards each call with your key, stores it locally and draws it on a live map.

title: System One for Apple Foundation Models
summary: A Swift bridge that brings decision models into Apple's Foundation Models framework.
how_jev_is_used: Evaluates typed Swift structs and enums against app state using Jev, or an on-device model when offline.

title: Jev: what is this viral decision model? (with a mini reproduction)
summary: Explores Jev and builds a small local reproduction to test the idea.
how_jev_is_used: Goes beyond an overview: the author trains a tiny local model in Jev's style to see how the approach behaves.

title: Jev explained (in Hindi), with a live demo
summary: A Hindi-language tutorial on Jev with a live demo.
how_jev_is_used: Explains the model and runs it live, in Hindi.

title: jev-chat: a reply assistant that reads the chat first
summary: Before you reply, it works out what the other person means and how risky the moment is, then drafts replies you can fill in with one tap.
how_jev_is_used: Jev judges intent and risk from the conversation on screen and helps pick the draft. Sending is always left to the person, and there are versions for Android, Windows, macOS and iOS.

title: JevChat for Windows: reply help beside the chat window
summary: A Windows companion that reads the conversation on screen and offers three candidate replies.
how_jev_is_used: Local OCR reads the messages, Jev judges intent and mood, and one click fills a reply into the input box. Sending is always manual.

title: JevHarness: let a language model write a harness for Jev
summary: A framework where a language model writes a task-specific harness around Jev, then the harness runs without it.
how_jev_is_used: The harness turns observations into features, builds Jev questions and criteria, and combines the answers into actions. It can be improved with rewards and full execution traces.

title: jev-chat for macOS: an on-screen reply assistant
summary: A read-only floating panel for macOS that explains what the latest message really means.
how_jev_is_used: It reads the chat window, then shows the likely intent, a risk level from 0 to 9 and suggested replies, using a local model and Jev. The author reports 86.4% on eight intent classes zero-shot.

title: Jev Chat Assistant: reply help for Windows chat apps
summary: A non-intrusive layer that reads the conversation on screen and suggests replies.
how_jev_is_used: Jev judges the other person's real intent, a danger level and the best action, then a generative model drafts three replies that Jev ranks. Sending is always manual. The page is mostly in Chinese.

title: Jev workflow builder: a multiplayer demo
summary: A demo of a collaborative workflow builder for Jev built with Liveblocks.
how_jev_is_used: You wire Jev and language models together, call the workflow through a REST API, preview test runs and see other people's cursors.

title: Laya vs Jev: two models play the T-Rex game
summary: A side-by-side game where a local Laya model and hosted Jev both play Chrome's T-Rex.
how_jev_is_used: It shows each model's choices, response times, survival streaks and crash replays on a shared course.

title: JEV DataOps: choose what data to keep, then fine-tune
summary: An open-source workbench for selecting and scoring data for a training run.
how_jev_is_used: Jev decides which records to keep, then the tool fine-tunes a model and compares results, saving every decision, split and report.

title: Jev as Policy: MuJoCo robot control studio
summary: A reproduction of a public control structure where Jev acts as a robot's policy.
how_jev_is_used: Text state becomes a Jev intent, then motor choices, then inverse kinematics in MuJoCo, with recording and a studio-style web panel. The demo task is to grasp an orange.

title: Jev with Claude Code: a how-to from RoboNuggets
summary: A short tutorial on adding Jev to a Claude Code setup.
how_jev_is_used: Shows how a coding agent can hand quick decisions to Jev. The creator links a free guide in the description.

title: Will Jev replace LLMs? A look at TypeSafe's model
summary: A video that asks whether decision models replace language models.
how_jev_is_used: Explains what Jev is, how it differs from an LLM and where each fits.

title: Diogo Almeida on why he couldn't build Jev at OpenAI
summary: A long interview with TypeSafe's co-founder and CEO.
how_jev_is_used: Covers his path from instruction-following models at OpenAI to building a model aimed at real work automation.

title: LangChain: building a harness with Jev
summary: LangChain's introduction to using Jev inside an agent harness.
how_jev_is_used: Describes Jev as a System One model and shows how it can handle classification-style decisions in an agent loop. The speed and cost figures are the company's claims.

title: CoderOne: an open-source, faster Jev
summary: A video about the open-source Laya model that appeared days after Jev's launch.
how_jev_is_used: Explains the System 1 idea behind Jev and what the open alternative offers.

title: AI Jason: Jev with Treg for automation
summary: A workflow demo combining Jev with the Treg tool catalogue.
how_jev_is_used: Walks through an automation built from Jev decisions and Treg tools.

title: AI Workshop: Jev with Claude Code and GPT-6 Astra
summary: A tutorial on connecting Jev to Claude Code and GPT-6 Astra.
how_jev_is_used: Shows the setup and a free guide from the creator's community.

title: Dave Ebbelaar: Jev explained for Python developers
summary: A Python-focused explainer with runnable examples.
how_jev_is_used: The examples are in the creator's public ai-cookbook repository.

title: Cole Medin: Jev and a new class of models
summary: A video on how to actually use Jev in practice.
how_jev_is_used: Argues that Jev is different from other launches because it cannot write a word, and shows what to use it for.

title: Raúl Marín: Jev for designers (in Spanish)
summary: A Spanish video on Jev from the point of view of product design and design systems.
how_jev_is_used: Explains how Jev makes semantic decisions compared with traditional language models.

title: Sean's AI Stories: Jev versus LLMs in 22 minutes
summary: An explainer that frames Jev as System 1 against System 2 thinking.
how_jev_is_used: Covers the launch, the model's evaluations and how it compares with LLMs.

title: Searching 6,000+ YC startups in under a second
summary: A search app over thousands of Y Combinator companies.
how_jev_is_used: Jev ranks startups by colour, niche, competitor, age or logo image. The author reports sub-second results and $2.70 of total testing costs.

title: A Chrome side panel that drives WebMCP tools with Jev
summary: A Chrome extension that operates a site's WebMCP tools from a side panel.
how_jev_is_used: On every keystroke Jev picks the right tool, fills in the arguments and says how sure it is. The demo does grocery shopping.

title: JevGrep: code search for agents, CLI and MCP
summary: Finds code by behaviour when an agent doesn't know the file or symbol name.
how_jev_is_used: Jev scores every eligible code fragment against the question and returns the original excerpts with paths and line numbers.

title: Jev-Mem: agent memory with a fast controller
summary: A research project separating frequent memory decisions from deeper reasoning.
how_jev_is_used: A Jev-style controller organises memories and guides retrieval; a language model writes the final answer. Published with a paper.

title: jevals: evals and guardrails for agents
summary: Runs evals and guardrails on every agent trace instead of using an LLM judge.
how_jev_is_used: All the checks for a trace go to Jev in one request costing a few thousandths of a cent, fast enough to run inside the agent loop.

title: Spring AI TypeSafe
summary: A Java client for Jev with Spring AI integrations.
how_jev_is_used: Uses Jev as a model-as-judge, a guardrail, a retrieval post-processor and a tool index inside Spring AI.

title: Jev: full tutorial with code
summary: A full tutorial on Jev with an accompanying GitHub repository.
how_jev_is_used: Builds examples on screen; the code is published alongside the video.

title: Minecraft agent: a language-model planner with Jev at the controls
summary: An agent that plays Minecraft Java 1.16.5 and aims to beat the Ender Dragon.
how_jev_is_used: A GPT model plans and Jev selects the player actions. The author reports a run completing in 8 minutes 43 seconds.

title: Crush Monitor: reading the mood in a chat
summary: A small tool that analyses a conversation for emotion, intent and how well each reply landed.
how_jev_is_used: It shows the three most likely emotions and intents per line, a goodwill score and a grade for your replies. It supports Jev, OpenAI Decisions and text models, and runs on your own machine.

title: EmbodiedJev: a robot decision workbench
summary: A MuJoCo workbench for trying decision models on three simulated robot tasks.
how_jev_is_used: It compares local small models with Jev and other model APIs on observe, decide, execute and feedback loops, and shows speed and cost. The page is mostly in Chinese.

title: Jev DSH: a decision plugin for agent harnesses
summary: A plugin that brings Jev's structured decisions to DeepSeek Harness, OpenCode and Codex.
how_jev_is_used: Jev helps choose tools, skills and task owners and rates the quality of the output, while the original agent keeps planning and executing. The page is mostly in Chinese.

title: webctl: a smart web search tool for agents
summary: A command-line search tool for agents that saves tokens.
how_jev_is_used: It runs several web searches and has Jev score each result against the original query and goal, so the agent reads fewer tokens.

title: Dasheng: read English aloud and see which words you got wrong
summary: A practice tool that listens to you read an English passage and marks mispronounced words as you go.
how_jev_is_used: A streaming speech model listens and Jev judges each word, so wrong words turn red in real time and a total score appears at the end. The page is mostly in Chinese.

title: jevchat: a chatbot made from a model that cannot write
summary: A project that turns Jev into a chat model.
how_jev_is_used: At every step it asks Jev which symbol comes next, using an alphabet plus a stop option, and samples from the returned probabilities.

title: Jimothy: turn your Jev usage into small local classifiers
summary: A tool that trains small, very fast classifiers from Jev-compatible examples.

title: Jev as a Judge with Comet Opik

how_jev_is_used: It replays ten synthetic support traces, including invented policies and a prompt-injection attempt, and runs deterministic checks first.

title: RoboJEV: two-stage Jev control of a Franka robot arm
summary: A small robotics lab that controls a simulated Franka Panda arm.
how_jev_is_used: Jev receives structured simulator state rather than images, picks an intent, then picks directions, and code does the motion maths.

title: jev-design: can a model design a dashboard?
summary: An experiment where a console's whole design system is generated by Jev from a one-sentence brief.
how_jev_is_used: You type a brief such as an eighteenth-century printed book and the dashboard restyles itself a second or two later.

title: Theo on Jev: a fast classifier with safety built in
summary: A long reaction and demo video about Jev from the creator behind t3.gg.
how_jev_is_used: Describes Jev as a fast classifier that does not replace reasoning models such as Astra or Fable, with demos of what it is good at.

title: Sam Witteveen: seven open Jev-style models
summary: A review of open models that copy the Jev approach.
how_jev_is_used: Goes through seven of them to see how good they are and what they can do.

title: Prompt Engineering: build RAG with Jev
summary: A walkthrough of using Jev to fix the reranker step in retrieval.
how_jev_is_used: Includes a Colab notebook and links TypeSafe's announcement post.

title: Smart copy and paste, powered by Jev
summary: A demo where copy and paste understands what you are doing.
how_jev_is_used: Marcus Lowe built it with Jev and describes it as a glimpse of computer interactions being rewritten.

title: Sorting years of Twitter bookmarks with Jev
summary: A demo of Jev working through a large pile of saved bookmarks.
how_jev_is_used: The author describes it as light work for Jev.

title: jev-use: let Jev take the steps that need no text
summary: A plugin for Claude Code, Codex and Pi that hands decision-only steps to Jev.
how_jev_is_used: When a step only needs a decision, Jev takes it; when text must be written, the LLM takes over. The author measures about 230 ms and $0.02 per 1,000 judgements.

title: jgrep: grep for what code does
summary: Semantic code search with no index or embeddings, plus a mode that picks which tests a diff can affect.
how_jev_is_used: Jev answers a yes/no question for each piece of code. The author reports scanning a src/ tree in about two seconds for roughly a cent.

title: sys1grep: grep by meaning, across languages
summary: Searches files by meaning and can find English text from a Japanese query, and the reverse.
how_jev_is_used: Jev scores every line against a meaning; meanings can be combined with AND, OR and NOT.

title: jev-lint: lint what a parser can't check
summary: Lint rules written as questions, such as 'does this comment match what the function does?'
how_jev_is_used: Jev answers each rule's question with a probability, catching mismatches between comments, types and behaviour that ordinary linters miss.

title: jev-use: say it, and your Mac does it
summary: Voice and typed computer use for macOS that reads the screen without screenshots.
how_jev_is_used: The app reads the screen through the Accessibility tree and Jev picks the next on-screen action.

title: Jev Desktop for Codex
summary: Adds a bounded decision loop to Codex's computer use for browser tabs and Mac apps.
how_jev_is_used: Codex sets the goal and allowed actions, Jev selects an operation and target in one request, and Computer Use performs it.

title: jev-align: AI functions from your feedback
summary: An experimental CLI that builds calibrated AI functions from human labels.
how_jev_is_used: Finds the examples Jev is unsure about, asks you to label them, and improves the function's questions automatically.

title: Jev × WebMCP Chrome extension
summary: Turns what you type into WebMCP tool calls on the current page.
how_jev_is_used: Jev reads the page's tool schemas and predicts the tool and its arguments as you type, with confidence and latency shown.

title: DocJev: fast document classification and splitting
summary: A library, command-line tool and local app that classify and split PDF, Word and PowerPoint document packets.
how_jev_is_used: Local text extraction feeds Jev, which predicts a document's category or the boundaries between documents using rules written in plain language.

title: Jev Code Reviewer: review behaviour, not just diffs
summary: A command-line reviewer and agent skill that ranks each change in a review as P0, P1 or P2.
how_jev_is_used: Jev prioritises what deserves human attention and only P0 changes show by default, while OpenAI explains the changes in plain language.

title: Jev Arena: Jev against DeepSeek on the same comments
summary: A tool that compares two models' speed, cost and labels on the same batch of comments.
how_jev_is_used: It imports CSV or Excel, replays the run and writes offline reports. The author reports 10,000 comments done in 203 seconds for $0.84 with Jev against 824 seconds for an estimated $1.50 with DeepSeek, with Jev slightly lower on accuracy. The page is mostly in Chinese.

title: oxlint-plugin-jev: lint rules in plain English
summary: An experimental Oxlint plugin where each rule is a yes or no question about code.
how_jev_is_used: Each match is sent to Jev with the question, and the plugin reports an error when the yes probability clears your cutoff.

title: Jev tried on 12 real use cases
summary: A hands-on test of Jev across a dozen automation use cases.
how_jev_is_used: Nate Herk runs Jev on practical business tasks and gives his verdict on where it helps.

title: David Ondrej: building with Jev
summary: A half-hour walkthrough of building things with Jev.
how_jev_is_used: Shows Jev used in practical builds and explains where it fits.

title: Jack Roberts: Jev AI just dropped
summary: An early look at Jev after launch.
how_jev_is_used: Introduces Jev and links a free skill for giving agents quick decisions.

title: Drape: real-time virtual try-on hauls
summary: An experiment where Jev picks outfits from a closet while you talk.
how_jev_is_used: Jev reads the transcript and what the person is wearing, picks from the closet and changes the outfit in real time. The author reports about $0.0011 and 620 ms per decision.

title: A synthetic focus group that scrolls 723 ads
summary: A marketing experiment where Jev scrolls ads as 30 buyer personalities.
how_jev_is_used: The author reports 21,690 stop-or-scroll decisions for 22 cents.

title: Classifying Zillow listings by things you cannot filter
summary: A demo of natural-language search over property listings.
how_jev_is_used: Jev classifies listings by architecture, renovation status or proximity to freeways. The author reports under 20 seconds and $0.18 for thousands of listings.

title: A viral post analyser run on 100,000 posts
summary: A tool that judges the structure of viral X posts.
how_jev_is_used: It asks 14 yes/no questions per post. The author reports 100,000 posts in 20.4 seconds for $0.67, against 214 posts in the same time with a larger model.

title: Tagging X posts in real time with Jev
summary: A feed filter that labels posts as breaking, golden nugget or slop.
how_jev_is_used: Jev tags each post as it arrives.

title: Jev on the Venice API: 24,000 Hacker News posts
summary: A demo classifying Hacker News posts into 12 categories.
how_jev_is_used: The author reports about two minutes for 24,000 posts.

title: A research dashboard for 1,315 X posts
summary: A dashboard that labels saved posts across eight dimensions.
how_jev_is_used: Jev labels topic, hook and writing style, so posts can be filtered by what they have in common. The author reports about $0.086 for 1,315 posts.

title: Clonk: launching agents on a canvas instantly
summary: An agent orchestrator that skips the slow language-model loop for routing.
how_jev_is_used: Jev launches agents on a canvas instantly, which the author credits for making it fast.

title: Tool calling that starts before you finish speaking
summary: An experiment replacing the language model's tool-choice step with Jev.
how_jev_is_used: Jev picks the tool instead of an LLM, which the author found lets the agent act before the user finishes the sentence.

title: Automatic model choice for image and video generation
summary: Picks the best-suited image or video model for each prompt on the Higgsfield API.
how_jev_is_used: Jev evaluates the prompt and selects the most fitting generation model from Higgsfield's catalogue.

title: Controlling Figma by voice
summary: Spoken commands drive Figma directly.
how_jev_is_used: Jev maps each spoken command to a Figma action. The author reports a total cost of one cent from first line of code to the recorded demo.

title: jev-pruner: trim long command output
summary: A Claude Code plugin that trims noisy Bash output before the model reads it.
how_jev_is_used: Short output passes through untouched; for long output, Jev picks the lines that matter so later turns carry less noise.

title: Shell history suggestions ranked by Jev
summary: Fish-style autosuggestions for zsh that guess which past command you're typing.
how_jev_is_used: As you type, Jev looks at your last 100 distinct commands and picks the one you're most likely completing, even when you describe it in words.

title: Jev Voice: talk to your Mac
summary: Speak and the Mac opens apps, types, searches, scrolls and presses keys.
how_jev_is_used: Speech is transcribed locally; one Jev call of about 250 ms turns the transcript into a typed action and its arguments.

title: Jev Social: social media research agent
summary: Turns Instagram, TikTok and LinkedIn into source-cited reports through your own browser.
how_jev_is_used: Jev chooses each next step (search, open a post, read comments or finish) and a local CLI carries it out in Chrome.

title: jevcache: a decision cache
summary: Caches Jev decisions locally so repeated questions are free and replayable in CI.
how_jev_is_used: Treats each decision as a function of model, questions and input, and memoises it; your key never leaves your machine.

title: ruby_decision_model
summary: A Ruby gem for decision models such as Jev, with no runtime dependencies.
how_jev_is_used: One client talks to Jev through OpenRouter by default or TypeSafe's API directly.

title: I tested Jev: here's what you can build
summary: Remixes projects from X: tweet scoring, ad research, Chrome extensions and a voice-controlled game.
how_jev_is_used: Walks through how Jev works, how to get access, and rebuilds several community demos.

title: Jev vs Claude and GPT on simple tasks
summary: Compares Jev with Claude and GPT on simple decision tasks.
how_jev_is_used: You give Jev text and a list of allowed answers; it returns a probability for each, and the video compares that with chat models.

title: Jev Browser Use: Jev clicks, Codex checks
summary: A browser skill that hands navigation, clicks and scrolling to Jev while Codex keeps text input and the final check.
how_jev_is_used: The authors report browser operations about 5 to 10 times faster in their own EZCollegeApp workflows.

title: Hermes Jev Skills: a second brain for the small decisions
summary: Skills that give coding agents a cheap, fast judge for decisions such as which model should answer.
how_jev_is_used: Jev handles model routing, memory, compaction, skill selection and browser actions for Hermes agents, and the skills also work with Claude Code and Codex.

title: tax-doc-classifier: sorting tax document pages with Jev
summary: A classifier that labels each page of a tax document as one of 261 IRS forms and 7 page kinds.
how_jev_is_used: One request per page goes to Jev, which returns probabilities. The authors report 100% classification of their own corpus at about $0.001 per page, 34 times cheaper and 6 times faster than their earlier language-model pipeline.

title: JevRouter: a lightweight router for models, tools and subagents
summary: A router that treats models, subagents, skills, tools and plugins as one candidate set.
how_jev_is_used: Jev answers one typed Choice question about which should handle the next step, and the router enforces availability, permissions, risk and confirmation around the answer.

title: jev-gateway: Jev chooses the tool, your LLM does the rest
summary: A local gateway for coding agents that asks Jev which tool to call.
how_jev_is_used: When the agent is about to choose a tool, the gateway asks Jev instead of the expensive reasoning model. Everything else goes to the usual model, and it works with Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode and Kilo.

title: Jev Chat: a command bar that calls tools without an LLM
summary: A chat-shaped command bar that calls real tools while no language model writes anything.
how_jev_is_used: Each turn a classifier picks what was asked, which tool, which argument values and whether to confirm, and code builds the reply from the tools' own data.

title: jev-rules: only the rules that matter, per prompt
summary: A Claude Code add-on that shows Claude only the standing rules that apply to each prompt.
how_jev_is_used: Jev decides which of your rules are relevant to the current request.

title: jev-paint: paintings from Jev's pixel probabilities
summary: A small local app that turns Jev's probability distributions into paintings.
how_jev_is_used: Jev returns pixel probabilities, which the app renders into images in the browser.

title: hono-jev-router: route requests by meaning
summary: An experimental router for the Hono web framework.
how_jev_is_used: You describe a request in plain words and Jev decides which description fits the incoming request.

title: Jev Recruiter: a LinkedIn recruiting agent
summary: A local recruiting workspace that browses LinkedIn profiles against a role.
how_jev_is_used: It is built on Browser Use's Jev Ultrafast; Jev chooses where to go, screens titles and assesses visible profile excerpts, and you keep the profiles and evidence.

title: Jev explained in seven minutes
summary: A short explainer on what Jev is and why TypeSafe built it.
how_jev_is_used: Covers the idea behind a model that returns decisions instead of text, and where it sits next to reasoning models.

title: Jev is here: how to use it, with Ryan Vogel
summary: A podcast-style walkthrough of Jev as a model built for classification.
how_jev_is_used: Ryan Vogel shows how Jev takes an input and an output schema and returns a probability for each choice.

title: Ray Amjad: Jev with Claude Code for a cheaper coding loop
summary: A tutorial on using Jev alongside Claude Code.
how_jev_is_used: Shows Jev handling routine decisions so the large model is used less often.

title: Hunter Bohm: pairing Jev with Astra
summary: A video on combining Jev with a large reasoning model.
how_jev_is_used: Shows what changes when Jev makes the quick calls and the large model plans.

title: Gary Explains: Jev is fast and cheap, but not an LLM
summary: An explainer on why Jev is fast and cheap and what the catch is.
how_jev_is_used: Explains that it understands natural language but replies with structured answers.

title: Jev plays Smash Bros against itself
summary: A demo where Jev controls all four characters in a fighting game.
how_jev_is_used: The author reports over 22 million tokens for the match at a cost of a couple of cents, with decisions in a fraction of a second.

title: Generating game levels in real time with Jev
summary: A game-development experiment where Jev produces levels as you play.
how_jev_is_used: The author argues that faster, cheaper structured output could matter for game development.

title: Keystroke oracle: a launcher that reads intent
summary: A predictive app launcher that re-ranks results on every keystroke.
how_jev_is_used: Jev reads intent, so typing the pdf I just downloaded puts the newest PDF on top. It is the first of Nader Dabit's Jev experiments.

title: Matching a candidate to 400 companies in 12 seconds
summary: A job-matching demo that scores companies against one candidate profile.
how_jev_is_used: The author reports 12 seconds and $0.0005 to predict the best-fitting jobs, with a confidence score and mismatches flagged.

title: A doomscrolling filter: Jev reads three days of posts
summary: A free tool that turns a niche's posts into a filtered feed.
how_jev_is_used: Jev asks eight questions about each post, removing bait and hidden ads and judging the text and engagement ratios. The author reports about two seconds and $0.007.

title: An always-on voice assistant with no wake word
summary: A computer assistant that listens all the time and decides when you are talking to it.
how_jev_is_used: Jev uses probabilities to tell a command from idle talk, which the author says makes an ambient assistant possible.

title: SEO and GEO audits that cost 90% less
summary: A write-up of agents that audit and fix a client's SEO and GEO.
how_jev_is_used: The author reports the cost dropping from about $250 per audit, with Jev speeding up reads of Search Console and analytics data and the analysis of which sources AI assistants cite.

title: A Mac app that files your downloads by rule
summary: A macOS app that watches the Downloads folder and applies customisable rules.
how_jev_is_used: Jev decides whether a file is an invoice, for example, and the app moves it and renames it, with no other model calls.

title: End-to-end testing with agents and Jev
summary: An open-source framework for running end-to-end tests with agents.
how_jev_is_used: It supports web and mobile and uses Jev for the decisions.

title: A used-goods hunter built with Playwright and Jev
summary: An agent that searches second-hand listings and acts on them.
how_jev_is_used: The author, writing in Spanish, reports about 26 listings a minute at roughly 406 ms a decision, with a total search cost of $0.00085, including messaging sellers when details are missing.

title: Intent-based search in Gmail
summary: A demo of searching an inbox by what you mean.
how_jev_is_used: Jev judges relevance to the intent, and the author suggests letting embeddings pull candidates first for a very large inbox.

title: Lurk: monitor Reddit threads to get cited by AI
summary: A free service that finds and monitors Reddit threads, aimed at getting your brand cited by AI assistants.
how_jev_is_used: The author reports 4,000 threads scanned with alerts by email, Discord and Slack, and says Jev makes the free tier possible.

title: Cline's Jev browser plugin
summary: A plugin that gives Jev a browser inside Cline.
how_jev_is_used: Install jev-browser from the plugin marketplace, add a Vercel AI Gateway key and ask for a browser task; Cline launches Chrome in the background.

title: An image classifier with OCR and Jev
summary: A small tool that sorts images by what they contain.
how_jev_is_used: The author reports about 900 images categorised in 40 seconds.

title: A two-arm robot controlled with Jev
summary: A robotics write-up in Japanese where Jev handles one layer of a three-layer control system.
how_jev_is_used: Jev takes the decision layer while code handles inverse kinematics and physics. The author reports 500 ms responses and about 0.5 yen per trial.

title: Website to App: turn a URL into a native mobile app
summary: A service that builds a native mobile app from a website address.
how_jev_is_used: Jev decides how to rebuild the site as a native app, then a shipping tool submits it to the app stores. The team says it has used it internally for iOS and Android apps.

title: keep.md: Jev for reranking and tagging
summary: A test of Jev on Cloudflare Workers for a bookmarking product.
how_jev_is_used: The author reports search reranking 7 times faster than the hybrid approach and tagging 50 times faster than a small LLM with no failures.

title: Monitoring 25 WhatsApp groups with Jev
summary: A real-time monitor for client groups.
how_jev_is_used: Jev judges urgency, problems and unresolved orders, and tells a language model to message the owner when something needs attention. The author writes in Spanish.

title: A prompt box that picks the agent, model and computer
summary: A personal tool that fills in the fields of a prompt box automatically.
how_jev_is_used: Jev picks the agent, model, computer and folder; a major rewrite goes to a large model with Claude Code and iOS changes run on one of his Macs.

title: A Slack agent made twice as fast
summary: A write-up of speeding up a Slack agent.
how_jev_is_used: Jev first classifies the best skill, tool and parameters for the prompt before handing it to the agent, which the authors say made it twice as fast.

title: talkr: a speech coach built on Jev
summary: A speaking-practice app.
how_jev_is_used: It gives you a topic and you talk for 30 seconds, then Jev analyses pauses, filler words, repetition, confidence and clarity and gives a score and feedback.

title: A voice computer assistant with a Swift accessibility app
summary: An early computer assistant that acts on what you say.
how_jev_is_used: Local Whisper transcribes, Jev classifies the action, and a small Swift app supplies the screen's accessibility tree. The author says it would be fully private if Jev ran locally.

title: Jev Search
summary: A free, open-source search engine you query in plain language.
how_jev_is_used: Jev decides where to search for each question and ranks the results that come back from the search API.

title: Jev MCP server for agent harnesses
summary: A proof-of-concept MCP server that adds Jev to an existing agent setup.
how_jev_is_used: Agents call it to check claims against evidence, screen content before it enters their context and rank candidates by meaning.

title: Agent Router: pick the right coding agent for a task
summary: A command-line tool that chooses the coding agent, model and effort level for a task, then launches it.
how_jev_is_used: Fixed rules filter your subscriptions by quota; Jev ranks what's left for the task and picks the effort. The chosen agent (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode) starts in a Herdr pane.

title: Criteria-based model routing
summary: Very fast model routing driven by criteria you define.
how_jev_is_used: Jev scores each request against the routing criteria and the highest-scoring model handles it.

title: Stanley: a Jev-first coding agent
summary: A command-line tool for checking and understanding code changes, described in plain words.
how_jev_is_used: Jev routes each request to a workflow; the workflow gathers evidence and asks Jev small fixed-choice questions, and code makes the final call. A general agent is only used as a fallback.

title: Jev Review: quality scores for coding agents
summary: A local MCP server that gives coding agents continuous quality scores while they work.
how_jev_is_used: Jev scores code on independent dimensions such as correctness, complexity, tests and security; the agent stays responsible for fixing what scores low.

title: SkillRanker: the right skill for the next step
summary: A Rust CLI that ranks an agent's installed skills for the next step of a session.
how_jev_is_used: Jev evaluates the agent's live context against the available skills; SkillRanker adds session hooks, safeguards and local feedback.

title: Semantic tool routing for the Pi agent
summary: Activates only the tools and skills a Pi agent needs for the current prompt.
how_jev_is_used: Jev matches the prompt against registered tools and skill files, and is also exposed for typed yes/no, choice and score questions.

title: Building with Jev: an agent skill
summary: A skill that helps coding agents write and improve programs that call Jev.
how_jev_is_used: Covers question design, state structure, confidence thresholds and diagnosing questions that answer wrongly or with low confidence.

title: voice-browser: it acts before you finish the sentence
summary: Controls a real browser by voice, word by word.
how_jev_is_used: On every partial transcript, Jev answers a dozen questions (intent, target, is the command complete, is it destructive) in about 300 ms, and code decides whether to act, wait or ask.

title: Jev Trade: a live Hyperliquid desk
summary: A trading bot on Hyperliquid across five coins, with a public live view.
how_jev_is_used: Jev reads the order book every tick and answers buy, sell or hold; the bot places the order.

title: pg_typesafe: Jev from PostgreSQL
summary: A pre-alpha PostgreSQL extension that calls Jev from SQL.
how_jev_is_used: Exposes Jev's choice, yes/no and score questions as SQL functions for classification work inside the database.

title: A tiny ad blocker, for fun
summary: A Chrome extension that asks Jev whether each page element is an ad and removes it.
how_jev_is_used: The single judgement, 'is this element an ad?', is Jev's; everything else is plain code. The author is clear it's an experiment, not a real ad blocker.

title: Jev for Home Assistant
summary: Ask your house a question and get a number back you can automate on.
how_jev_is_used: Questions become sensors (a probability, a choice or a score), with actions for automations and a conversation agent.

title: fast-jev-compaction: smarter context compaction for Claude Code
summary: A Claude Code plugin that replaces the usual compaction summary with decisions about which tool calls to keep.
how_jev_is_used: Jev scores every tool call and result in one request. Stale ones are dropped or truncated, and everything kept stays word for word, so nothing is rewritten.

title: pg-jev: ask your Postgres tables questions in plain language
summary: A PostgreSQL extension that filters, ranks and classifies rows with conditions written in everyday words.
how_jev_is_used: Every row is judged by Jev, which returns calibrated probabilities, so there is no index, embedding or vector column to maintain.

title: Foreman: a supervisor for coding agents
summary: An agent supervisor that watches coding agents at work and decides what they should do next.
how_jev_is_used: It runs on decision models, supporting Jev and OpenAI's Decisions API, and can supervise workers such as Codex and OpenCode on a ticket or specification.

title: Unclutter: a browser extension that removes page clutter
summary: A browser extension that strips clutter from web pages using reusable template rules.
how_jev_is_used: Jev classifies the nonessential elements on a page, and the extension stores local hiding rules by page template and reapplies them on later visits.

title: System One Connector: Jev as an MCP tool
summary: An MCP connector that gives Claude Code, Codex and other agents direct access to Jev.
how_jev_is_used: The agent asks a question such as whether something is urgent or which team owns it and gets back a number or an option it can use in an if statement.

title: jev-browser: fast, cheap browser use with Jev
summary: A tool that drives a real headless browser through an MCP server, command line or library.
how_jev_is_used: Jev picks one action per step from the page's clickable, typeable and selectable elements and scores how likely the goal is met or the run is stuck. Code owns the loop.

title: skillbox: a self-hosted skills library for agents
summary: A versioned skills library for AI agents that serves skills over MCP.
how_jev_is_used: It offers optional Jev recommendations for which skill an agent should use.

title: Kill My Idea: Jev judges your startup idea
summary: A web tool where you describe a startup idea and get KILL IT, FIX IT or SHIP IT.
how_jev_is_used: One request asks Jev ten questions in parallel, eight scored from 0 to 4 plus the category and clarity. A weighted average and a clarity gate produce the verdict, with no generative model.

title: JevPilot: a driving simulator with a Jev autopilot
summary: A playable Three.js driving simulator with Tesla Autopilot-like behaviour.
how_jev_is_used: Jev makes the driving decisions through a hosted endpoint that requires a login. The project offers a small amount of free Jev play credit.

title: compact-adviser: should you run /compact now?
summary: An agent plugin that answers one question: is it safe to compact this session?
how_jev_is_used: Jev judges whether the session is at a boundary where compaction is safe, then hints at it or, on Pi and Claude Code if you opt in, runs it for you.

title: fastbrowse: a fast browser agent with cited answers
summary: A browser agent that runs locally or in a cloud browser and returns cited answers or validated data.
how_jev_is_used: Jev picks from indexed page controls, so it cannot click something that was never on the page, while a language model reads and plans.

title: Sponsor Skip: a Chrome extension that skips YouTube sponsor reads
summary: A Chrome extension and web app that find sponsor reads in a video and jump past them.
how_jev_is_used: Jev names the transcript line or answers yes or no about what it heard, and code owns every timestamp. It needs a TypeSafe key.

title: jev-mcp: Jev as tools for coding agents
summary: A local MCP server that gives Cursor, Codex and other clients typed Jev judgments.
how_jev_is_used: It routes the next step and decides whether a partner model is needed, while the host agent still edits files and runs commands.

title: Syntax: Jev explained with demos and use cases
summary: CJ explains what Jev is and how it works, then goes through several use cases and demos.
how_jev_is_used: The code for the jev-chat demo is public on GitHub.

title: Maximilian Schwarzmüller on Jev
summary: A short reaction video on a model that beats LLMs in some areas.
how_jev_is_used: Gives a developer's first impression of Jev.

title: Moritz: Jev full tutorial
summary: A twenty-two minute tutorial on Jev, a model built for fast decisions.
how_jev_is_used: Walks through setup and examples.

title: AICodeKing: Jev with Browser Use
summary: A test of Jev driving a browser agent.
how_jev_is_used: Tests Jev as a System One model for fast, cheap, structured decisions and shows how fast the agent is.

title: Breaking down 724 live ads in 40 seconds
summary: An ad-analysis demo that breaks down hundreds of live ads at once.
how_jev_is_used: The author reports 724 ads from 37 brands covered in 40 seconds for about nine cents of tokens, labelling each ad's hook, format, offer, call to action, awareness stage and landing-page mismatch.

title: Jev plays Subway Surfers, 50 games at once
summary: A demo of Jev playing a fast arcade game and running 50 games at once.
how_jev_is_used: The author reports the run cost less than a cent and notes that Jev does not replace large reasoning models.

title: Giving Jev $10,000 to trade
summary: A video experiment where Jev makes trading decisions with real money.
how_jev_is_used: The author says they gave Jev $10,000 and let it trade.

title: SuperX: score a post for virality, then rewrite
summary: A free tool that scores a draft post before you publish it.
how_jev_is_used: Each post gets 61 questions in about a second. The author reports it was fitted on 9,481 real posts from 207 creators and picks the more viral post two times in three.

title: Rebuilding the X algorithm with Jev
summary: A simulator that predicts how a post would perform on X.
how_jev_is_used: It uses real ranking weights, simulates a post's virality and has a global feed where you see everyone.

title: Jev plays Slay the Spire 2
summary: A demo of Jev playing a card game faster than a human can follow.
how_jev_is_used: The author, writing in Chinese, reports about 0.7 seconds of thinking per action, compared with a slower run using GPT-6 Astra.

title: A live viral post analyzer
summary: A tool that analyses a draft as soon as you pause typing.
how_jev_is_used: Half a second after you stop, Jev scores the post's viral potential and categorises it live. The author calls it an experiment.

title: Fraud detection: Jev first, Kimi for the uncertain cases
summary: A pipeline that classifies emails with Jev and sends unsure ones to a larger model.
how_jev_is_used: The author reports 100 emails classified in 1.42 seconds, and 96 of 100 correct for about $0.07 once uncertain cases went to Kimi K3.

title: Stagehand with Jev: browser use for a tenth of a cent
summary: A fast browser-use loop built with Stagehand.
how_jev_is_used: The page's accessibility tree goes to Jev as state, Jev picks the next action and Stagehand carries it out. The authors report a task costing $0.001.

title: What works on X: 3,282 posts analysed
summary: An analysis of one creator's posts across 100 million views.
how_jev_is_used: Each post got eight questions about topic, hook and tone. The author reports 4.25 million tokens for $0.128, and that how-to posts got a median of 150 likes against 44 overall.

title: A visual reference finder
summary: A tool that turns one prompt into 100 reference images.
how_jev_is_used: It draws on Cosmos, NASA and The Met, with Jev selecting what fits the brief.

title: Ask Jev Anything
summary: A website that does not answer questions but judges them.
how_jev_is_used: It runs on Jev and Convex, and the author set a goal of one million questions.

title: Jev Detector: a fast AI-slop checker
summary: A free tool that scans text for AI slop.
how_jev_is_used: The author reports about 10,000 words scanned in about two seconds, with no sign-up.

title: A Wikipedia link-walking agent with Jev
summary: A demo of an agent navigating with Jev and headless Chromium.
how_jev_is_used: It walks from the Café page to Inteligencia artificial by following links. The author, writing in Spanish, reports completing it in 20 seconds.

title: fx.sh: agentic browsing in a Chrome extension
summary: A Chrome extension that lets agents browse and click in your own browser.
how_jev_is_used: Decision-making by Jev, with Vercel AI Gateway.

title: Jev as a chief of staff for bots
summary: An agent orchestration demo where Jev picks the right teammate for a task.
how_jev_is_used: Jev reads the task, wakes the right agent and gives each the right model, on OpenMausBot.

title: Real-time Clippy with Jev
summary: A helper that watches how you use a product and wakes up when you struggle.
how_jev_is_used: It notices hesitation, confusion and getting stuck, and even its reactions are controlled by Jev.

title: Classifying company invoices for accounting
summary: A use case showing Jev sorting invoices into accounting categories.
how_jev_is_used: The author, writing in Spanish, says a company's invoices can be reviewed and classified in seconds.

title: pi-jev: a decision layer for the Pi agent
summary: Adds Jev to the Pi coding agent as a gate on risky tool calls and a fast way to ask typed questions.
how_jev_is_used: Jev judges bash, write and edit calls before they run, reads command output, and answers the agent's own questions through a jev_ask tool.

title: blink: codebase search with walkers
summary: Searches a codebase with an ensemble of walkers that move through the file tree.
how_jev_is_used: At each folder, Jev chooses which way to walk toward the file that answers the query.

title: jev-browser: an LLM plans, Jev decides
summary: Browser automation as a library, CLI and MCP server.
how_jev_is_used: For each step, one Jev request picks the element, the action and the value, and checks whether the step is done, blocked or about to do something irreversible. Playwright performs it.

title: neo4jev: navigating a graph
summary: A demo that walks a Neo4j graph one hop at a time toward a goal.
how_jev_is_used: At each node, the outgoing relationships become Jev choices, and a yes/no question in the same call asks whether the goal has been reached.

title: SemDecide: decisions for Unix pipelines and CI
summary: Pipe in text and get a predicate, route, score or filtered stream with a stable exit code.
how_jev_is_used: Jev answers the semantic question; SemDecide handles the parsing, retries and confidence thresholds.

title: JEV breakdown: the first AI model built for code
summary: An early breakdown of Jev on launch day: what it is and why developers took notice.
how_jev_is_used: Covers the System One idea, typed answers and probabilities, and what that means for software.

title: Jev: the schema-safe AI for automation
summary: What changes when an AI model stops generating text and returns schema-safe answers instead.
how_jev_is_used: Explains typed decisions and why they matter for automation pipelines.

title: Jev Ultrafast: a browser agent that picks each click
summary: A browser agent from the Browser Use team that works toward a goal one fast step at a time.
how_jev_is_used: Jev picks an operation and an element from an indexed list of page controls, and a small language model writes text only when text has to be typed. The authors report a Zürich to London flight search on Google Flights in 7.1 seconds.

title: jev-trader: one trade decision per Monad block
summary: A trading bot that asks Jev whether to buy or sell on every block of the Monad chain.
how_jev_is_used: Jev reads the Kuru MON-USDC order book and answers buy or sell about every 300 ms, and each block posts a post-only limit order on that side. Without a private key it runs as a dry run with simulated fills.

title: typesafe-computer-use: Mac computer use for a fraction of a cent a step
summary: A tool that drives a Mac toward a goal typed in plain English.
how_jev_is_used: The screen is read with OCR and a small classifier picks the next action. A writing model is called only when a text field needs free text. The author reports about $0.0002 per step.

title: jev-router: model routing for Claude Code and Codex
summary: A command-line wrapper that picks a fast or strong model for each turn.
how_jev_is_used: Jev sends simple work to the fast tier and difficult work to the strong tier, while each tool keeps its own interface, sessions and login.

title: Perch: semantic code linting with decision models
summary: A command-line scanner that checks code against meaning-based rules rather than patterns.
how_jev_is_used: Each code unit is judged by a decision model and decisions are cached, so scanning unchanged code again is free.

title: winnow: a context sieve for Claude Code
summary: A plugin that judges every large tool result before it enters Claude's context.
how_jev_is_used: Blocks the judge is confident you don't need are replaced with a short stub and a key that restores the full text on demand.

title: Classifying 1,500 of his own emails with Jev
summary: A test of Jev on a real inbox.
how_jev_is_used: Vogel ran 1,500 of his own emails through Jev and reports being impressed by the accuracy.

title: A playable Jev demo on Val Town
summary: A live demo anyone can try.
how_jev_is_used: Steve Krouse built it as a quick way to see how Jev behaves.

title: Meet Jev: the AI built to make decisions
summary: A launch-day first look at Jev and a first build with it.
how_jev_is_used: Shows a first project built on Jev's decisions.

title: QuantDinger: an open-source trading workbench with a Jev option
summary: A self-hosted stack for turning trading ideas into Python strategies, backtests, paper trading and live execution.
how_jev_is_used: A Jev pre-trade decision gate checks each proposed trade before it goes ahead, as an alternative to a gate that relies only on a language model.

title: TipTour: a local computer-use companion for the Mac
summary: A macOS menu bar companion that carries out click-based tasks you type.
how_jev_is_used: In its Jev mode, Jev chooses from controls detected locally on the screen, and the app executes and validates each action.

title: ThoughtDAG: a canvas for AI conversations, with Jev retrieval
summary: An infinite-canvas app where AI conversations branch into a graph and the wires carry the context.
how_jev_is_used: An optional Jev decision layer helps identify topics and rank relevant excerpts from earlier agent sessions and canvases, and your chosen language model writes the answer. The authors report a median of 391 ms for Jev in a small relevance pilot.

title: VexJoy Agent: routing plain-English requests to specialist agents
summary: A toolkit of agents, skills and hooks that turns a plain request into the right workflow.
how_jev_is_used: Its /do command uses Jev for intelligent routing, then gates the work with reviews and tests.

title: AI Stock: a research workspace with an optional Jev decision engine
summary: A website for researching stocks, comparing investing views and testing strategies with simulated money.
how_jev_is_used: Jev can act as an optional buy, sell or hold decision engine inside the simulator.

title: Canny: no 'done' without evidence
summary: A supervision layer for Claude Code and Codex that won't let an agent finish on an unproven claim.
how_jev_is_used: Deterministic hooks keep a ledger of what the agent actually did and make the decisions; Jev advises on the judgement calls.
